hook.situation: You sit down at a 삼겹살 restaurant with coworkers, order by servings, ask for side dishes and rice, grill meat at the table, cut it when it is cooked, and pack leftovers.
objectives: Order Korean barbecue with 인분, 공기밥, 밑반찬, and N 주세요.
Talk about table grilling with 굽다, 익다, 자르다, and V아/어 주세요.
Describe taste and reasons with 맵다, 짜다, 신선하다, -아서/어서, and -(으)니까.
hook.whyItMatters: Korean food culture is not just food names. At many meals, you order shared portions, cook at the table, ask for refills, and explain taste or cooking stage before making a request.

grammarNotes.title: N 주세요 — ordering an item
grammarNotes.mentalModel: Use this for the thing you want brought to the table: meat, rice, side dishes, water, or a menu.
grammarNotes.formation: Put the food item before 주세요. Add numbers and counters when needed: 삼겹살 두 인분 주세요, 공기밥 하나 주세요. Add 좀 for a softer refill request.

examples.en: Please give us two servings of samgyeopsal.
Please give us one bowl of rice.
examples.note: 공기밥 is the restaurant rice item.

examples.en: Please give us a little more side dishes.
Please give me just a little ssamjang.

exceptions: N 주세요 asks for an item. For an action, use V아/어 주세요: 잘라 주세요, 포장해 주세요.

grammarNotes.title: V아/어 주세요 — asking for an action
grammarNotes.mentalModel: Use this when you want the staff or someone at the table to do something, not just bring an item.
grammarNotes.formation: Make the 아/어 form of the verb and add 주세요. 자르다 becomes 잘라 주세요, 포장하다 becomes 포장해 주세요, 굽다 becomes 구워 주세요.

examples.en: The meat is cooked, so please cut it.
Please pack the leftovers to go.
examples.note: Natural at the end of a meal.

examples.en: Please grill the garlic together too.
The broth is hot, so please be careful.

exceptions: 굽다 has the spoken form 구워요/구워 주세요. Do not say 굽어 주세요.

grammarNotes.title: V고 — linking food actions
grammarNotes.mentalModel: Use this to list what happens at the table: order, grill, eat, and then add rice or pack leftovers.
grammarNotes.formation: Attach -고 to the verb stem. 굽다 becomes 굽고, 먹다 becomes 먹고, 볶다 becomes 볶고. It can simply list actions or show a loose sequence.

examples.en: We grill the meat and grill the garlic together too.
We eat samgyeopsal and also order fried rice.
We boil the broth and grill meat too.
examples.note: Two cooking actions in one sentence.

examples.en: We pack the leftovers and go home.

grammarNotes.title: V/A아서/어서 — reason and result
grammarNotes.mentalModel: Use this when the taste, heat, or ingredient quality explains what happens next.
grammarNotes.formation: Use -아서 after many ㅏ/ㅗ stems and -어서 after other stems; 하다 becomes 해서. In this chapter, use it for plain results: 매워서 밥을 같이 먹어요, 신선해서 맛있어요.

examples.en: The seasoning is spicy, so I eat it with rice.
The broth was salty, so I drank a lot of water.
The meat is tasty because it is fresh.
The meat was cooked, so we ate it right away.
examples.note: A result statement, not a command.

exceptions: For a request or suggestion, use -(으)니까 more naturally: 고기가 익었으니까 잘라 주세요.

grammarNotes.title: V/A(으)니까 — reason for a request or suggestion
grammarNotes.mentalModel: Use this when the reason comes first and the next sentence is a request, suggestion, or warning.
grammarNotes.formation: Add -니까 after a vowel stem and -으니까 after a consonant stem. With past tense, use -았/었으니까: 익었으니까. This is very useful at restaurants because reasons often lead to requests.

examples.en: The meat is cooked now, so please cut it.
The side dishes are not enough, so please give us more.
The ssamjang is salty, so put in only a little.
The broth is hot, so eat slowly.

exceptions: Use -아서/어서 for plain results, but -(으)니까 before requests and suggestions.

readingText.title: 삼겹살 두 인분 주세요
readingText.body: 민서는 회사 사람들과 삼겹살집에 갔어요. 먼저 삼겹살 두 인분하고 공기밥 하나를 주문했어요. 밑반찬이 부족해서 직원에게 밑반찬도 좀 더 달라고 했어요. 고기를 굽고 마늘도 같이 구웠어요. 고기가 익었으니까 먹기 좋게 잘라 달라고 했어요. 양념이 조금 매워서 공기밥을 같이 먹었고, 쌈장은 짜니까 조금만 넣었어요. 마지막에는 남은 음식을 포장해 달라고 했어요.
readingText.bodyTranslation: Minseo went to a samgyeopsal restaurant with coworkers. First, Minseo ordered two servings of samgyeopsal and one bowl of rice. Because the side dishes were not enough, Minseo asked the staff for more. They grilled the meat and garlic together. When the meat was cooked, Minseo asked someone to cut it into easy-to-eat pieces. The seasoning was a little spicy, so they ate it with rice, and since the ssamjang was salty, they added only a little. At the end, they asked to pack the leftovers.

comprehensionQuestions.answer: 양념이 조금 매워서 공기밥을 같이 먹었어요.

culturalNote.title: Shared food, shared actions
culturalNote.body: At many Korean barbecue restaurants, the meal is shared at the table. People order meat by 인분, grill it together, ask for 밑반찬 refills, and often eat meat with 상추, 마늘, and 쌈장. The language follows the workflow: N 주세요 for items, V아/어 주세요 for actions, and -(으)니까 when a reason leads to a request.
culturalNote.tip: Keep 굽다 and 익다 separate: 사람이 고기를 구워요, but 고기가 익어요.

inlineExercises.explanation: 인분 counts food servings. 명 counts people.

inlineExercises.explanation: 굽다 takes the meat as object; 익다 uses the food as subject.

inlineExercises.explanation: 포장해 주세요 asks the restaurant to pack leftovers to go.

bullets: Core flow: order by 인분, add 공기밥, ask for 밑반찬, grill meat, cut it when cooked, and pack leftovers.
굽다 is the cooking action; 익다 is the food becoming cooked.
N 주세요 orders an item; V아/어 주세요 requests an action.
-아서/어서 explains a plain result, while -(으)니까 works well before a request or suggestion.
